carbon.sci.intro: Software Carbon Intensity says how much carbon one unit of your application costs: SCI = ((E × I) + M) / R. E, I and M come from the period on screen; you tell it R, what the application delivered.
carbon.sci.limit_average: Intensity is the location-based average of the grid, not marginal; energy is estimated from usage, not metered.
carbon.sci.limit_boundary: The boundary is the cloud usage the platform ingests for the selected period and project; software outside it (devices, networks, on-premises) is not counted.
carbon.sci.limit_embodied_in: Embodied emissions (M) are part of the total; the split between E × I and M is not shown.
carbon.sci.limit_embodied_out: The active methodology does not include embodied emissions (M = 0), so this SCI is operational only and understates the full figure.
carbon.sci.limit_unit: The result is only as meaningful as R: use one unit you can count the same way every period, and compare like with like.

method.title: Methodology
method.subtitle: Where the numbers come from, how they are calculated and what they do not include.
method.immutable: A methodology version is immutable: a new set of coefficients is a new version, and old results are never rewritten.
method.none: No calculation has used a methodology yet.
method.f.energy: energy (kWh) = usage quantity × energy coefficient of the service × PUE
method.f.carbon: CO₂e (kg) = energy (kWh) × grid intensity (gCO₂e/kWh) of the region and hour ÷ 1000
method.f.sci: SCI = ((E × I) + M) ÷ R, per functional unit R; M (embodied) is 0 until it is sourced
method.f.note: Where no usage quantity exists, a cost-based factor is used and the row is labelled as such. Coefficients of the active version are listed in its provenance.
method.sources_intro: For each day the first source in this order that has enough readings is used. Sources are shown side by side and are never averaged together.
method.src.electricitymaps: Measured hourly intensity of the electricity grid by zone, with forecasts. The primary source; past data depends on the plan.
method.src.uk: Hourly national intensity of Great Britain from the system operator, with forecasts. Free; used for GB regions.
method.src.eia: Computed, not measured: hourly net generation by fuel of a US balancing authority (EIA-930) with generic life-cycle factors per fuel; imports between authorities are not accounted for.
method.src.ember: Monthly national averages. A coarse fallback that fills days without hourly readings and is always labelled as a monthly average.
method.l.operational: Emissions are operational (electricity of the workloads). Embodied carbon of hardware is not included.
method.l.estimate: Figures are estimates. Energy comes from coefficients, not from metering, unless a measured source is connected.
method.l.history: Hourly history exists from the moment a source was connected; earlier days use the monthly fallback or stay empty.
method.l.relocation: A cleaner region reduces operational emissions only if the workload can run there: price, latency, data residency and availability must be checked.
method.l.units: Per-unit figures are shown only for the days the customer reported units of work, and only when all selected projects count the same unit.
method.src.energy_charts: Computed, not measured: public generation by production type of a European country (Energy-Charts, Fraunhofer ISE; data of the transmission system operators, CC BY 4.0) with generic life-cycle factors; cross-border flows are not accounted for. Has history, no key.
method.src.ieso: Computed, not measured: Ontario's public hourly generation by fuel (IESO) with generic life-cycle factors; imports are not accounted for. Used behind a source that publishes a measured intensity.
method.src.hydroquebec: Computed, not measured: Quebec's open hourly generation by source (Hydro-Québec) with generic life-cycle factors; imports are not accounted for. The open history ends on 2025-12-31; later days come from the live feed as it is collected.

info.kpi_cost: What your connected clouds billed in the selected period, in your reporting currency. Read from each cloud's own cost data and checked against the cloud's totals. The small line is the daily average and how the last 7 days compare with the 7 before.
info.kpi_intensity: How much CO₂e one kilowatt-hour of the electricity under your workloads emitted, averaged over the period and weighted by the energy used. Lower is cleaner. Grid data comes from the sources shown in Data quality.
info.fin_forecast: Where this month's cost will end: what has been spent so far plus the average daily cost of the last 7 days for the days that remain. A projection, not a bill.
info.fin_budget: The share of your monthly budget already used, and the month-end projection against it. Set a budget in Settings to get warnings before it is exceeded.
info.fin_anomalies: Days whose cost is unusually far from what the recent pattern predicts (more than three standard deviations). Needs about two weeks of data.
info.fin_per_currency: Grams of CO₂e emitted for every unit of currency spent. A single number that links the FinOps and the GreenOps view: falling is good.
info.trend: Daily cost (blue, left axis) and operational CO₂e (green, right axis). Move over the chart for a day's values. Dots mark days with unusual cost. The 7-day average smooths the weekly rhythm.
info.split: Where cost and emissions come from, as shares of the total: by cloud or by region. Each region carries the carbon intensity of its grid, so an expensive region is not always a dirty one.
info.services: Every service ranked by cost. The two bars are its share of cost (blue) and its share of emissions (green). "Carbon-heavy" marks a service that emits far more than it costs. The trend compares the second half of the period with the first.
info.regions: Click a region on the map or in the list. The map shows the grid intensity of each region; the panel explains what it means for you: your cost and CO₂e there, how the grid moved, and what a move to a cleaner region would change.
info.regions_yours: The regions where you have resources in this period, with the CO₂e of what runs there. These are the ones a recommendation can move out of.
info.efficiency: Cost and CO₂e per unit of work (requests, builds, jobs) that you report for a project. Shown only for the days units were reported, never extrapolated.
info.quality: How far the figures can be trusted: whether cost matches the cloud's own totals, and how much of the grid data is a day average rather than the latest known value.
info.setup: What is still missing for the full picture, in the order it helps. Each step explains what it unlocks; the list disappears when everything is set up.
info.recs: Ideas the platform found in your usage, ranked by the carbon they could save per month. They are proposals: a person approves each, and nothing is changed for you.
info.accounts: The clouds and clusters feeding the platform and their state: connected and synced, waiting for the first sync, failing, or not connected.
info.activity: The latest things that happened in your organization: syncs, connections, reports and recommendations.
info.optimization: Estimated carbon reduction per month if the open recommendations were applied. It is an estimate, not a measurement: the measured effect is shown separately after a change is applied.
info.connectors_active: Connections and clusters that are delivering data now, out of everything connected.
info.connectors_sources: The kinds of source that deliver data: clouds and Kubernetes.
info.connectors_health: Of your connections, the share whose most recent finished sync succeeded. The bars in the list show the recent history.
info.connectors_time: How long a successful sync takes on average, from start to finish.
info.org_details: Your organization's name and the currency every cost figure is shown in. Only administrators can change them.
info.org_clouds: The cloud accounts the platform reads cost and usage from. Click one to connect it or to see how it is doing.
info.org_sources: Where grid carbon intensity comes from: how many regions each source covers and how fresh its latest reading is. "% of your data" is the share of your own figures it supplied.
info.org_policy: Budget and limits that turn into alerts. Click a row to change it in place. Alert thresholds warn before a budget or limit is reached.
info.org_automation: What the platform may do on its own. Region moves and rightsizing always need a person; time shifting can be allowed per project in its policy.
info.org_notifications: Where alerts and reports go. The switches enable or pause a channel's destinations; the single organization-wide switch is on the Notifications tab.
info.org_security: People, API keys and the audit log. Two-factor authentication and session length are managed by your sign-in provider.

proj.subtitle: Group cloud accounts and workloads, see what each project costs and set the rules it runs by.
proj.new_hint: A project groups the cloud accounts and workloads you want to measure together. The functional unit is what it produces (requests, builds, jobs): it turns totals into cost and CO₂e per unit.
proj.info.projects: The projects of your organization. Every cloud account, budget, policy and recommendation belongs to one.
proj.info.cost: What the projects cost together in the selected period, after your allocation rules have moved shared costs between them.
proj.info.regions: Projects that have allowed regions set. Without them no region-move recommendation can be made for a project.
proj.info.budgets: Budgets that are at risk of being exceeded or already exceeded.

info.alerts_list: Alerts the platform raised for your organization: budgets, anomalies, failed syncs and data gaps. Resolve or acknowledge them so the list stays meaningful.
info.alerts_anomalies: Days where spend jumped well above the recent normal for a service. Check what changed before it becomes the new baseline.
info.alerts_undelivered: Messages we could not deliver to a destination (a wrong address, a revoked webhook). Fix the destination in the delivery settings.
info.carbon_history: How dirty the electricity was in each region over time, in gCO₂e per kWh. Lower is cleaner; running work then and there emits less.
info.carbon_schedule: The hours of the next day when each region's grid is expected to be cleanest. Flexible jobs (batch, training, backups) belong there.
info.carbon_origin: Where each intensity value came from: a live reading, a published annual average or a fallback estimate. Measured readings are the most trustworthy.
info.carbon_totals: Energy, operational and embodied emissions and cost summed over the selected period, per cloud and currency.
info.carbon_daily: Emissions per day. A step change usually means a new workload, a region move or a change in the grid.
info.carbon_method: The version of the calculation methodology applied to these numbers and whether it is verified.
info.sci_calc: Software Carbon Intensity (SCI): emissions per functional unit, (energy × grid intensity + embodied) per unit of work. Try values to see how each lever changes it.
info.k8s_clusters: Kubernetes clusters that report energy for their workloads. Select one to narrow the workload table.
info.k8s_workloads: Energy and emissions per workload, attributed from node power by CPU and memory share. Use it to find the heaviest deployments.
info.method_current: The methodology version in force. Every figure in the platform is calculated by it and stays reproducible.
info.method_formulas: The exact formulas used for energy, operational and embodied emissions and SCI.
info.method_sources: Where the factors come from: power models, grid data providers and embodied-carbon datasets.
info.method_limits: What the numbers do not capture. Read before using them in an external report.
info.reports_new: Choose the report, the format and the period. Generation runs in the background and the file appears below when ready.
info.reports_list: Reports generated for your organization. Download them while they are available; each is kept for the retention period.
info.acc_connection: How this cloud account is connected, to which project it belongs and when it last synced.
info.acc_quality: Which kinds of data arrive for this account (billing, usage, energy) and how complete they are.
info.acc_fix: Steps that unlock the missing data for this account.
info.acc_sync: Every synchronization run with its result. Failed runs say why.
info.struct_report: Cost per project after your allocation rules: direct cost, cost allocated in and out, and the resulting total.
info.struct_teams: Teams own projects. Reports and budgets can be read per team.
info.struct_rules: Rules that split shared costs (a common cluster, a network) between projects by a fixed share or by usage.
info.set_members: People with access to this organization and the role each one holds.
info.set_invite: Invite a colleague by e-mail with a role. The invitation expires if not accepted.
info.set_pending: Invitations sent and not yet accepted. Revoke one if it was sent by mistake.
info.set_auto: Whether the platform may apply low-risk recommendations on its own. Off means everything waits for your approval.
info.set_auto_rules: Which kinds of change may be applied automatically and under what limits.
info.set_export: Download all the data of your organization in an open format.
info.set_erase: Permanently deletes the data of your organization after a confirmation. It cannot be undone.
info.set_keys: Keys let your tools call the platform API. Each key shows its scope and last use; revoke the ones you do not recognize.
info.set_keys_new: A new key is shown once. Store it in a secret manager; we keep only a hash.
info.set_policy: Per project: where it may run (data residency), what the platform may apply itself, the monthly carbon limit and the CI gate.
info.set_audit: Who did what and when in your organization. The record cannot be edited.
info.set_budgets: A monthly or quarterly spend limit per project. You are warned at the thresholds before it is exceeded.
info.set_notif_master: One switch for all outgoing notifications of the organization.
info.set_notif_dest: Where notifications go (e-mail, Slack, Teams, webhook) and which events each destination receives.
info.set_notif_add: Add a destination, then send a test message to check it works.
info.set_notif_hist: The latest messages with their delivery result.
info.set_group: A group of settings. A change applies to the organization and is written to the change history.
info.set_history: Every change of a setting with the person and the time, so a surprising behaviour can be traced.
info.set_plan: Your current plan, its status and what it includes.
info.set_plan_usage: How much of each plan limit you have used. Near the limit, change the plan before it blocks you.
info.set_plan_change: Switch to another plan. The change applies from the next billing period.
info.set_roles_custom: Roles you define: pick exactly which actions a role may perform.
info.set_roles_builtin: Roles every organization has. They cannot be edited; copy one into a custom role to adjust it.
info.set_prefs_display: How numbers, dates and language look for you only. It does not affect other people.
info.set_prefs_access: Accessibility options such as reduced motion and larger text.
wiz.name.title: What is the project called?
wiz.name.body: A project groups the cloud accounts and workloads you want to measure together: a product, a service, an environment. Pick a name your team will recognize.
wiz.unit.title: What does it produce?
wiz.unit.body: The functional unit is the thing the project delivers: a request, a build, a job. It turns totals into cost and CO₂e per unit, so you can see whether you are getting more efficient.
wiz.team.title: Who owns it?
wiz.team.body: Assign the project to a team so costs and budgets can be read per team. You can change this later.
wiz.team.empty: There are no teams yet. Create them in Teams & allocation.
wiz.review.title: Everything in place?
wiz.review.name: Name
wiz.done.title: {name} is ready
wiz.done.body: Next, give it something to measure. These three steps make its numbers real.
wiz.done.regions: Choose the regions it may run in
wiz.step.name: Name
proj.delete_hint: Its policy, budget and work units are removed. A project with cloud connections or data cannot be deleted.
cb.subtitle: What your cloud emits, the energy and the grid behind it, where it comes from, and the best moment to run flexible work.
cb.empty: No carbon data yet. Connect a cloud account and run a sync; emissions are calculated from its usage and the grid under each region.
cb.info.emissions: Operational CO₂e of the period: energy used times the carbon intensity of the grid each workload ran on. The change is against the previous period of the same length.
cb.info.energy: Electricity the workloads are estimated to have used, from usage and the hardware's power model. It is an estimate, not a meter reading.
cb.info.intensity: Energy-weighted average of how much CO₂e each kWh of the grid emitted where your work ran. Lower is cleaner.
cb.info.sci: Software Carbon Intensity: emissions per functional unit of the application. It needs the units your projects delivered, reported in Projects.
cb.info.breakdown: The same emissions split by cloud, by region (with the grid intensity of that region) or by service.
cb.trend.empty: A trend needs at least two days of data.
cb.break.title: Where it comes from
cb.hist.no_regions: No regions with carbon yet. Intensity history appears for the regions your workloads run in.
cb.hist.empty: No stored grid readings for {region} in this period. Readings are collected hourly from the configured sources; days without a reading stay empty.
cb.hist.sources: One source is used per day, in this order: {list} (at least {min} readings a day). Sources are shown side by side and never averaged together.
cb.hist.ember: Monthly national averages are from Ember (CC-BY 4.0).
cb.hist.few_body: Hourly readings are stored from the moment a source was connected; most plans do not return the past. The history is filled automatically from sources that provide it (Ember monthly averages, UK Carbon Intensity, EIA) once they are connected, and every day adds 24 more readings.
cb.origin.body: Share of the period's carbon whose grid intensity is the mean of that day's own readings. The rest uses fewer readings or the latest reading, which is less precise.
rp.title: Reports
rp.subtitle: Carbon, cost, SCI and the executive summary as files you can share: pick what, for which project and period, see the first rows, then generate.
rp.info.total: Every report generated for your organization that has not been deleted.
rp.info.ready: Reports whose file is ready to download.
rp.info.pending: Reports being prepared in the background. This page refreshes by itself.
rp.info.failed: Reports that could not be generated. Retry them; the reason is shown.
rp.info.new: A report is a table of the period's data in the format you choose. The preview below is built the same way as the file, so what you see is what you get; the file itself is prepared in the background.
rp.kind.carbon_hint: Energy, grid intensity and CO₂e per day, service and region.
rp.kind.finops_hint: Cost per day, service and region in your currency.
rp.kind.sci_hint: Carbon per functional unit on the days units were reported.
rp.kind.sustainability_hint: Totals, data quality, top services and regions, recommendations.
rp.kind.ghg_hint: Cloud services as Scope 3 category 1 in tCO2e, by provider, month and service, with data quality and what is not included.
rp.format.pdf: A formatted document to read or attach. Long tables are cut at {rows} rows.
rp.format.csv: A table for a spreadsheet, with every row.
rp.format.json: Structured data for your own tools, with every row.
rp.err.order: The end date must not be before the start.
rp.err.long: A report covers at most {max} days.
rp.preview_wait: Fix the period to see a preview.
rp.preview_empty: There is no data for this period and scope yet; the report would be empty.
rp.info.list: Reports of your organization, newest first. Download a ready file, retry a failed one, or delete one you no longer need (its file is removed too).
rp.delete_ask: Delete this report and its file?
rp.empty: No reports yet. Pick a kind above and generate the first one.
rp.progress_done: Ready — it is in the list below
au.title: Change pipeline
au.subtitle: From an approved recommendation to a reviewed plan, to a change you apply yourself and report. The platform prepares and records; it never touches your cloud.
au.info.safety: By design (ADR-0017) the platform builds the plan, the commands and the way back, and a second person approves it. You apply it with your own tools and report the result here, so your cloud access stays read-only.
au.rollback_title: What happened when you rolled it back?
au.empty.ready: No approved recommendation is waiting for a plan. Approve one in Recommendations and it appears here.
au.empty.review: No plan is waiting for approval.
au.empty.apply: Nothing approved is waiting to be applied.
cw.cloud.title: Which cloud do you want to connect?
cw.cloud.body: Reliabilix reads the costs and usage of an account to calculate its footprint. Pick the provider; you decide in the next step how access is given.
cw.readonly: Read-only by design: the platform never changes anything in your cloud.
cw.method.title: How should Reliabilix read {name}?
cw.method.body: Both ways are read-only. The first is the quickest; the second keeps every credential on your side.
cw.method.own.aws: Access key of a read-only IAM user
cw.method.own.aws_body: Create an IAM user that may only read costs and paste its access key once. The secret is sealed and never shown again.
cw.method.other.aws_body: No key is stored: you create a role that trusts Reliabilix with an External ID. More steps, nothing to rotate.
cw.method.own.azure_body: An app registration with the Cost Management Reader role on the subscription; paste its tenant, client and secret once.
cw.method.other.azure: Cost Management export in Blob Storage
cw.method.other.azure_body: Reliabilix reads the FOCUS export from your storage container; gives measured VM hours and never asks for a key.
cw.method.own.gcp_body: A service account with BigQuery Data Viewer on the billing export; paste its JSON key once.
cw.method.other.gcp_body: Share the billing export dataset with the platform's service account and label it. No key file is stored.
cw.details.title: Where is the account?
cw.details.body: Choose the project it belongs to and enter its identifiers. Each field is checked as you continue.
cw.sealed: The secret is stored sealed, used only to read cost data and never shown again. Remove the key or the role assignment in your cloud to revoke access at any time.
cw.sealed_other: No secret is stored for this way of connecting. Remove the role, the share or the export to revoke access at any time.
cw.verify.title: One last thing on the cloud side
cw.verify.retry: check the steps above, then try again.
cw.setup.aws_key: Make sure the IAM user of this key can read the costs of AWS account {id}:
cw.setup.azure_sp: Give the service principal read access to the costs of subscription {id}:
cw.setup.gcp_key: Make sure the service account of the key can read the billing export of project {id}:
cw.setup.aws_role: Create an IAM role in AWS account {id} that trusts Reliabilix, using this External ID:
cw.setup.azure_export: To read the Cost Management export of subscription {id}, do these steps:
cw.setup.gcp_share: To read the billing export of project {id}, do these steps:
cw.setup.token_azure: Container ownership token (set as metadata, value = 1)
cw.done.title: {name} is connected
cw.done.body: Access works. The first sync starts shortly and the numbers appear on the Overview as soon as data arrives.
k8.subtitle: Energy of workloads as measured in your clusters. It is part of the cloud energy already counted on the Overview and is never added to it: this page shows where inside the nodes the energy goes.
k8.stat.carbon_wait: some hours wait for grid data
k8.stat.low_hint: use under a quarter of the request
k8.info.clusters: Clusters whose agent has reported energy in the selected period.
k8.info.energy: Energy the workloads were measured to use (Kepler), before PUE.
k8.info.carbon: Measured energy times the grid intensity of each hour. A dash means some hours have no grid reading yet; the carbon appears once they do.
k8.info.oversized: Workloads that use under a quarter of the CPU or memory they request: candidates for smaller requests.
k8.info.by_ns: Energy of the workloads shown, grouped by namespace.
k8.info.top: The workloads that used the most energy in the period.
k8.rs.title: Right-sizing ideas
k8.info.rs: Recommended requests are the highest hourly usage of two weeks plus 25 % headroom. The platform changes nothing in the cluster; you apply it and mark it applied.
k8.rs.note: It frees reserved capacity; fewer nodes follow only if the scheduler can pack better, so no saving is claimed. Hourly averages hide spikes: check them first.
k8.wl.title: Workloads
k8.low_tip: Uses less than a quarter of what it requests: a candidate for smaller requests
k8.no_grid: Some hours have no grid data yet
k8.foot: Measured energy (Kepler) × PUE × grid intensity of that hour. Use is what the workload consumed of what it requested over the hours the agent reported both; it is the base for right-sizing.
k8.setup.none: No Kubernetes data yet. Run the agent in a cluster and its workloads appear here.
k8.setup.s1: Create an API key for the agent: the wizard below does it in one click, nothing to fill in Settings.
k8.setup.s2: Run the agent next to your Prometheus: the reference script, or the packaged CronJob from the guide.
k8.setup.s3: Within the hour the first cluster and its workloads show up here.
k8.setup.keys: Create the key and the manifest
kc.cluster.title: Which cluster?
kc.cluster.body: The platform never reaches into your cluster. A small agent in it reads Kepler from Prometheus once an hour and pushes the energy of each workload. Tell us how to label it.
kc.f.name: Cluster name (a stable one)
kc.f.api: Reliabilix API address (optional, you can fill it in later)
kc.err.name: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, up to 63 characters.
kc.err.region: A region id such as eu-central-1, westeurope or europe-west4.
kc.push_note: Push, not pull: the agent only sends numbers out with a key that may do nothing else. No cluster credentials are given to the platform.
kc.key.title: A key for the agent
kc.key.body: The agent authenticates with its own API key of the access “Kubernetes agent”. It is shown once; we keep only a hash.
kc.key.scope: This key can only send Kubernetes energy for your organization. Revoke it any time in Settings.
kc.install.title: Install the agent in the cluster
kc.install.body: Run the two blocks in a namespace next to your Prometheus. The agent runs every hour and sends the last complete hour.
kc.install.req: Needs Kepler exporting to Prometheus (and kube-state-metrics for requests). Full guide: docs/setup/kubernetes.md.
kc.wait.title: Waiting for the first hour
kc.wait.body: As soon as the agent has pushed an hour, {name} appears here. This can take up to an hour; you can close this and come back.
kc.done.title: {name} is sending data
kc.done.body: The cluster is connected. Its workloads and their energy are on this page now.
cd.subtitle: The carbon and cost gate for your pipelines: set the limits per project, ask the gate from a pipeline or from here, and see every decision it made.
cd.info.checks: How many times a pipeline (or you, from this page) asked the gate in the selected period.
cd.info.pass_rate: Share of checks whose planned change stayed within the limits.
cd.info.warned: Checks that came close to a limit; the change may go on, but is worth a look.
cd.info.blocked: Checks that went over a limit. The carbon shown is what the blocked changes would have added each month: a change not made, not a measured saving.
cd.try.title: Try the gate
cd.info.try: The same call a pipeline makes. Describe a planned change (vCPU-hours, memory or storage in a region); the gate estimates its monthly carbon with the grid of that region, adds the cost you give and compares both with the limits.
cd.try.hint: Only increases count: a change that reduces carbon or cost never blocks. The check is recorded in the history below.
cd.try.empty: Describe a change and check it: the verdict and its reasons appear here.
cd.verdict.PASS: Within the limits: the change may go ahead.
cd.verdict.WARN: Close to a limit: review before merging.
cd.verdict.BLOCK: Over a limit: the pipeline should stop.
cd.res.no_thresholds: No limits are set for this project, so the gate can only report the estimate. Set them on the right.
cd.res.operational: Operational emissions only; embodied emissions are not modelled.
cd.pol.title: Limits per project
cd.info.policies: The default limits the gate applies when a request does not bring its own. Carbon limits are kg CO₂e a month the change adds; cost limits are in your currency.
cd.int.title: Connect a pipeline
cd.info.integrate: A pipeline calls POST /ci/evaluate with an API key of the access “CI gate only”. The key can do nothing else, so it is safe to keep in the pipeline's secrets.
cd.int.no_keys: No CI key yet. Create one and keep it in your pipeline's secrets.
cd.int.fresh_note: It is shown once; we keep only a hash.
cd.int.scope: The key can only ask the gate and the schedule.
cd.int.snippet_note: Replace the API address with yours and put the key in a secret named RELIABILIX_API_KEY. Adjust the change to what the pipeline deploys.
cd.hist.title: Decisions
cd.info.history: Every check, whether from a pipeline or from this page, with the verdict and the reason.
cd.hist.none_match: No decision with this verdict in the period.
cd.hist.empty: No checks yet in this period. A pipeline's calls and your tests above appear here.
bl.info.current: The plan your organization is on now, its status and when the paid period ends. Limits and modules follow the plan.
bl.free_note: The Free plan has no end date.
bl.expired_note: The paid period has ended. Renew to keep the plan; until then Free limits apply to new resources.
bl.soon_note: The paid period ends soon. Renew now so nothing is interrupted.
bl.info.plans: Every plan with what it includes. Moving up applies as soon as the payment is confirmed; moving down never deletes anything, it only stops new resources over the smaller limit.
bl.free_current: You are on the free plan.
bl.free_after: What you return to when a paid period ends.
bl.not_sold: Not available online yet. Contact the platform operator.
bl.info.order: What you are about to pay for. The plan travels to the payment provider, so its confirmation tells the platform exactly which plan to activate or renew.
bl.intent.renew: A renewal of your current plan
bl.intent.downgrade: A move to a smaller plan
bl.order.note: You will be taken to the payment provider's page. The plan changes when the provider confirms the payment; this page updates by itself when you come back.
bl.order.downgrade_note: Nothing is deleted. Resources above the smaller limits keep working, but you cannot add new ones until usage is under the limit.
bl.order.upgrade_note: The new limits and modules apply as soon as the payment is confirmed.
bl.waiting: Waiting for the payment provider to confirm {plan}. This can take a minute.
bl.info.history: Checkouts you started and payments the provider confirmed for your organization.
bl.history_none_access: Billing history is available to owners, admins and billing users.
bl.ev.requested: Request for {plan} sent to the platform operator
bl.near_limit: You are close to a limit of your plan.
roles.give_hint: Optional: you can also change anyone's role later in Members.
roles.tpl.finops_desc: Costs, budgets and reports; no changes to cloud accounts.
roles.tpl.sustainability_desc: Carbon, calculations, reports and applying recommendations.
roles.tpl.developer_desc: Sees projects and carbon, uses the CI gate, reads automation plans.
roles.tpl.auditor_desc: Reads everything, including the audit log; changes nothing.
settings.tabdesc.organization: Overview and what to set up
settings.tabdesc.security: API keys and the audit log
bell.empty_body: Important messages and alerts will appear here.
nc.title: Notifications
nc.subtitle: Messages the platform sent, alerts that need a decision, cost anomalies and deliveries that failed. Only things worth your attention come here.
nc.info.messages: Important events of your organization: payment reminders, reports, change plans, recommendations. What appears here is set in Settings, Notifications.
nc.info.alerts: Conditions that need a decision (budget, carbon limit, a broken connection). Acknowledge one to say you have seen it, or mute it.
nc.info.anomalies: Days where spend jumped well above the recent normal.
nc.info.delivery: Notifications that could not be delivered to a destination.
nc.messages.empty: No messages. Important events will appear here.
nc.alerts.empty: No alerts here. Budgets and connections are checked every hour.
nc.anomalies.empty: No cost anomalies in this period.
bs.bell_hint: What people of the organization see inside the product.
bs.info.bell: Messages from the platform appear in the bell and on the Notifications page. These settings decide which ones, and they apply to what is already there.
bs.show_hint: Turn off to keep the bell for alerts only.
bs.sev.info_hint: All events, including good news such as a finished report.
bs.sev.warning_hint: Things that need attention; routine confirmations stay out.
bs.sev.critical_hint: Only what cannot wait. Billing messages are still shown.
bs.sound_hint: A soft chime while the page is open. Each person can switch it off for themselves in the bell.
bs.admins_only: Only owners and admins can change this.
bs.billing_hint: Reminders before the paid period ends and receipts.
bs.info.billing: Reminders go to the bell and, as a copy, to the e-mail of owners, admins and billing users. Each reminder is sent once per period.
bs.remind: Remind me before the end of the paid period
bs.remind_hint: A reminder {days} days before, another close to the end and a last one the day before.
bs.remind_off_hint: No reminders. The plan simply returns to Free when the period ends.
bs.copy_hint: Send reminders and payment receipts to owners, admins and billing users by e-mail.
bs.types_hint: Switch off the kinds you do not need in the bell.
bs.info.types: Billing messages cannot be switched off: a missed payment reminder is the one thing nobody wants hidden.
operator.header.subtitle: Platform administration
plan.card.title: Plan
plan.card.hint_free: More projects, connections and modules on a paid plan.
cb.kpi.energy_cost_based: Estimated from cost ({pct}% of it), not metered
rec.latency_hint: The round trip from {from} to {to} ({km} km). {basis}. Within your limit of {budget} ms. Check it for what users wait on: it is region to region, not from your users.
rec.compare_note: Regions beyond your latency limit ({budget} ms) are listed but never proposed. Change the limit in Settings → Cost & carbon policies. Cost is known only where the price index covers both regions.
ov2.reg.blocked_latency: cleaner regions exist, but all are beyond your latency limit
lat.title: Latency a move may add
lat.hint: How far a recommended region may be from where the workload runs now.
lat.body: A cleaner or cheaper region is proposed only if the round trip to it is no longer than this. Farther regions are still shown as options, marked as beyond the limit. Raise it for batch work that does not care; lower it for what users wait on.
lat.note: An estimate from the distance between the regions (about 1 ms per 65 km, there and back), not a measurement. It applies at the next daily analysis.
act.title: Recent Activity
act.empty: Nothing has happened yet. Connect a cloud account and the platform starts to fill this in.
ov2.pl.title: Move check
ov2.pl.note: Each figure says where it comes from: measured by Microsoft or CloudPing between the two regions, or estimated from the distance (with its typical error). There is no measurement for Google Cloud or between clouds. The same lines are drawn on the map. Where it is within your limit and the grid is cleaner, a move is realistic.
ov2.pl.verdict_yes: Realistic to move from {from}: about {ms} ms away, {pct}% cleaner grid.
ov2.pl.verdict_no: Nothing you run is both within {ms} ms of this region and on a cleaner grid.
lat.basis.measured_azure: Measured by Microsoft (Azure inter-region round trip)
lat.basis.measured_aws: Measured by CloudPing (AWS inter-region, median over a year)
method.src.entsoe: Computed, not measured: actual generation per production type from the ENTSO-E Transparency Platform with generic life-cycle factors; cross-border flows are not accounted for and pumped storage is left out. It needs a free security token and ranks behind sources that publish a measured intensity.
method.src.ons: Computed, not measured: Brazil's open hourly energy balance by subsystem (ONS: hydro, thermal, wind, solar) with generic life-cycle factors. The dataset does not split thermal generation by fuel, so one assumed factor stands for the thermal mix; distributed generation and imports are not accounted for.
map.national: gCO₂e/kWh · 0 – 600+ · lighter: national monthly average (Ember) · faint: inventory, direct emissions, at least this much
ov2.reg.now_note: Now: the middle of the last six hours. Recommendations compare the typical value of the last 7 days, so a short spike does not decide a move.
au.dry.ready: Ready: applying this plan now would be allowed
au.dry.note: Nothing was run or changed. This is a check of the plan against the current state.
au.dry.held: Held back on purpose (enable by hand later)
au.dry.c.commands_safe: Every command has a safe shape
bl.list_price: List price; the payment provider sets the final amount.
rs.title: Scheduled reports
rs.info: A report that makes itself every week or month. The people you choose get an e-mail with a link when it is ready; the file stays behind the sign-in.
rs.empty: No schedules yet. Set one up and the report arrives in your inbox without a request.
rs.cadence.weekly_hint: Every Monday at 06:00 UTC, for the seven days before.
rs.cadence.monthly_hint: On the 1st at 06:00 UTC, for the whole month before.
rs.recipients_none: No members to pick from, or you may not list members. The report is still made; it appears in the list below.
rs.recipients_hint: Only members of the organization. Nobody is picked by default.
rs.delete_ask: Delete this schedule? Reports already made stay.
cm.title: What a commitment would save
cm.info: A report, not a purchase. It looks at the compute and database spend day by day, takes the level the spend stays above on 80% of days, and shows what committing to part of it would save at the discount you enter.
cm.lead: Cloud providers sell a discount for promising to spend a steady amount for one or three years. This page finds the steady part of your bill and shows the saving and the risk. Nothing is bought here: take the figures to your cloud console.
cm.coverage: Share of the steady spend to commit
cm.coverage_hint: Lower is safer: the rest stays flexible.
cm.risk: If the capacity is not fully used
cm.break_even: A commitment is paid whether it is used or not: below {pct}% use it costs more than on-demand. {stable}% of the committable spend sits at or under the steady level. Discount shown for a {term}-year term.
cm.baseline_note: Steady level: {value} a day (reached on 80% of days)
cm.not_enough: Only {days} days of spend so far: at least 14 are needed for a steady level that is not a guess.
cm.maybe_committed: The amortized price differs from the billed one: part of this spend may already be under a commitment. Check the cloud console before buying more.
cm.empty: No compute or database spend in this window yet. Connect a cloud account and wait for the first sync.
cm.window: Days {from} to {to}, compute and database only, in your reporting currency.
cm.caveat: The discounts are planning figures (typical ranges for a flexible plan), not a quote: the real rate depends on the instance family, region, payment option and your agreement, so replace them with the rate your console shows. The baseline is measured on billed spend; storage, network and other services are not committable here. Savings are on-demand equivalents and before tax.
ff.title: What we found
ff.lead: Your first sync is in. Here is what it is worth.
ff.saving_hint: Open recommendations with a known price, a year at the monthly rate. Excludes commitments.
ff.carbon: Carbon you could cut a year
ff.carbon_hint: Modelled reduction of all open recommendations, a year at the monthly rate.
ff.moves_hint: {unpriced} of them have no price estimate yet.
ff.commit_hint: Steady compute and database spend at a planning discount. A report: nothing is bought.
ff.note: Estimates, not promises: each move waits for your approval, and the saving is measured after it is applied.
sc.title: Create the access with code
sc.note: Creates a read-only credential for cost data only. Review it before you run it; the secret it prints goes into the form below and is stored sealed.
cw.hint.denied: The cloud refused the read. Check that the role or key has the permissions of the setup steps, then try again: new permissions can take a few minutes to apply.
cw.hint.not_found: The cloud answered, but the export or account was not found. Check the account id and the export name for typos.
cw.hint.no_data: Access works, but the first data has not arrived yet. Cost Explorer and billing exports can take up to 24-48 hours after they are turned on.
cw.hint.network: The platform could not reach the cloud just now. Try again in a minute.
dm.title: No cloud account yet? Look around with sample data
dm.body: Adds a project with 60 days of invented cloud spend, so you can see the dashboards, recommendations and reports working. It uses none of your connection limit, and one click removes it.
dm.active_title: You are looking at sample data
dm.active_body: The spend in the project "Sample data (demo)" is invented. Carbon figures and recommendations appear within a couple of minutes. Connect your own cloud to see the real thing.
ov2.fin.range_hint: 80% range from how far the same method missed on recent days.
ov2.fin.forecast_seasonal: {spent} so far; {days} days left, forecast by weekday pattern and trend
ov2.fin.lag: Days still arriving from the cloud ({count}) are counted as forecast.
ov2.fin.may_exceed: On track, but could reach {high}: the budget may be exceeded.
budgets.projected_hint: Seasonal forecast: weekday pattern and recent trend, with an 80% range.
ue.title: Unit economics
ue.info: What one unit of your work costs and emits, month by month. Only the days you reported units for are counted, and the unit is the one named in the project.
ue.lead: Cost and CO₂e per request, order, customer or whatever the project counts. The change compares the two latest months with at least seven reported days.
ue.basis: {month}: {units} units over {days} reported days. A faint bar is a month with fewer than 7 reported days.
ue.empty: No units reported yet. Report how many requests, orders or customers a project served, and its cost and carbon per unit appear here.

trust.title: Trust and security
trust.lead: What protects your data, what we do with it, and what is not finished yet. Written from how the platform works, not from a brochure.
trust.isolation.title: Every organization is isolated
trust.isolation.0: Your data sits in tables protected by row-level security that is forced for every tenant table. A request without an organization sees zero rows.
trust.isolation.1: Your role is read from the database on every request, not from the sign-in token, so removing a member or changing a role takes effect at once.
trust.isolation.2: The database roles of the API and the worker cannot bypass these rules and the audit log can only be added to.
trust.access.title: Who can do what
trust.access.0: Sign-in is OpenID Connect with multi-factor authentication at the identity provider. Machine access uses API keys that are stored only as a hash, shown once and revocable.
trust.access.1: Access is by role, checked on the server. Invitations are one-time, expire in 7 days and are tied to a verified e-mail address.
trust.access.2: The platform plans changes but never executes them in your cloud. A plan needs an approved recommendation and a second human approval; machine keys can never approve.
trust.cloud.title: How we reach your cloud
trust.cloud.0: Access is read-only and made by you: a role or service account with billing and usage read permissions, protected against the confused-deputy problem by an identifier unique to each connection.
trust.cloud.1: Where a secret has to be kept (for example a service principal secret), it is sealed with AES-256-GCM bound to your organization, can only be written, and never appears in a response, a log or an export.
trust.data.title: Your data and leaving
trust.data.0: We process billing and usage records and resource metadata. We do not read the content of your workloads or storage.
trust.data.1: The owner can export all of the organization's data at any time, and can delete the organization: after a grace period (14 days by default) it is erased in one transaction together with its files, and only a record of counts remains.
trust.data.2: Every change is written to an audit log in the same transaction as the change. Backups keep data until they age out.
trust.subprocessors.title: Services the platform can use
trust.subprocessors.1: Payment providers for plans: Stripe, Paddle, LiqPay, WayForPay or a payment link, depending on the deployment. They receive payment data; we do not store card numbers.
trust.subprocessors.2: Public grid-intensity sources (for example ENTSO-E, Energy-Charts, UK Carbon Intensity, IESO, Hydro-Québec, ONS) and, with a key, Electricity Maps. They receive only a region or zone, never your data.
trust.subprocessors.3: The final list for your deployment, with hosting, is part of the data processing agreement.
trust.honest.title: What we do not have yet
trust.honest.0: No independent penetration test and no SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certificate yet. The platform is in alpha.
trust.honest.1: Not yet in place: single sign-on through SAML (sign-in is OpenID Connect today; SCIM provisioning exists, see the security model), signed images with an SBOM, and a published backup retention period.
trust.honest.2: Emission figures use provisional coefficients and are not meant for a published statement yet; the Methodology page says which.
settings.invite.sent: Invitation e-mailed to {email}. If it does not arrive, pass the token below over a secure channel; it expires in 7 days and only works for that address.
settings.invite.nomail: E-mail is not set up on this platform, so nothing was sent: pass this token to the person over a secure channel. It expires in 7 days and only works for the invited address.
invite.title: You have been invited
invite.lead: Join the organization with the account you are signed in with. The invitation only works for the e-mail address it was sent to.
invite.missing: This link has no invitation in it. Open the link from the e-mail again.
invite.failed: This invitation cannot be used: it may have expired, been used already, or was sent to another e-mail address than the one you signed in with.
ov.rec.reason.same_price: The published list price of this capacity is the same in both regions: moving saves carbon and changes nothing in the bill.
rec.cost_basis_index: Estimated from the cloud's published on-demand list prices of a basket of sizes in both regions (excludes discounts, data transfer and migration).
rec.cost_basis_list: A rough estimate: the ratio of the cloud's published list prices of every meter this service has in both regions, not a basket of sizes. It does not know your usage mix; excludes discounts, data transfer and migration.
sb.title: Showback by cloud tag
sb.info: The cost of the selected period split by the values of a tag (label) your clouds put on resources. Cost without the tag is shown as untagged and is never spread over the others.
sb.lead: Who spends what: pick a tag key, for example team or environment. The percentage next to a key is how much of the bill carries it.
sb.key_hint: {values} values, {pct}% of the bill carries this tag
sb.empty: No tagged cost in this period yet.
sb.empty_hint: Tags are read at the next sync of each connection, for the keys chosen in Settings (team, env, project and similar by default). Earlier days are filled in when they are read again.
sb.coverage: {pct}% of the bill has a value for {key}
sb.untagged_hint: No value for this key: assign it in your cloud to see who spends it
sb.no_values: No cost carries the tag {key} in this period.
sb.basis: Billed cost in the reporting currency, per day and service as the cloud reports it. Carbon is not split by tag. Azure and Google Cloud are read through their cost and billing-export APIs, AWS through the FOCUS data export; a connection through Cost Explorer only has no tags.
sb.tags_from: Tags are stored from {date}: days before that count as untagged only because tags were not read then. Each sync keeps the last month of tags up to date.
connectors.item.datadog: Monitoring and logging cost from a usage or billing export (CSV)
connectors.item.snowflake: Warehouse and storage cost from a usage export (CSV)
connectors.item.custom-csv: A cost export of any SaaS or tool in CSV: a FOCUS export works as it is
imp.title: Costs of SaaS and other vendors
imp.info: Upload the cost export of a vendor that is not AWS, Azure or Google Cloud. It is added to your costs, per day and service, and can carry tags for showback. It has no carbon: a vendor outside the clouds has no region and no energy model, and none is invented.
imp.lead: Datadog, Snowflake, MongoDB Atlas, GitHub, a spreadsheet of your own: any CSV with a date and a cost. The columns are recognised by name. A later file for the same days replaces them; each file can be taken back.
imp.readonly: Uploading cost files needs the right to manage connections.
imp.accepted: Accepted: {rows} rows, {services} services, {total}, {from} to {to}. It is being added to your costs.
imp.format_body: A header row, then one row per day and service. Required: a date (ChargePeriodStart, Date, UsageDate ...) and a cost (BilledCost, Cost, Amount ...). Used when present: ServiceName, BillingCurrency, EffectiveCost, and tags (a Tags column with JSON, or columns named tag_team, label_env ...). Monthly figures are placed on the first day of the month.
k8c.title: What the cluster costs
k8c.info: The cost of the cluster's nodes, taken from your cloud bill, split over namespaces and workloads by what each holds of the nodes: the larger of what it requests and what it uses. Where the agent reports the nodes' capacity, what nobody holds is idle.
k8c.lead: Like a bill by namespace and workload: who holds the nodes, what part of that is idle, and what pays for requests nobody uses. Only the hours the agent reported are costed.
k8c.empty: No cluster has reported in this period, or there is no cloud cost in the project to split.
k8c.idle_unknown: unknown: the agent does not report the nodes' capacity yet
k8c.idle_hint: {pct} of the cost: nodes nobody holds
k8c.waste_hint: paid for, asked for, not used
k8c.pool_assumed: Assumed: every compute cost of the project is this cluster. Choose the services that pay for it.
k8c.pool_hint: Tick the billed services that are this cluster's nodes (for example Virtual Machines or Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud - Compute). Nothing ticked means every compute cost of the project.
k8c.unmeasured: {count} workloads reported energy but neither requests nor use, so they hold nothing and get no cost.
k8c.unallocated: {amount} of the cost fell on days where no workload held anything.
k8c.basis: CPU {cpu}% and memory {mem}% of the node cost; each shared by what workloads hold (the larger of request and use). Use over request below 30% is marked.
sso.title: Company sign-in (SSO)
sso.hint: Let your people sign in through your company's identity provider.
sso.info: Claim your e-mail domain, prove it with a DNS record, and name the Auth0 connection (SAML or OIDC) your people sign in with. From then on the sign-in page sends addresses of that domain to that connection. Optionally a person who signs in with a verified address of the domain joins on their own with the role you choose.
sso.dns: Publish this TXT record in the DNS of the domain, then check. DNS changes can take a few minutes.
sso.readonly: Only owners and administrators manage company sign-in.
sso.note: The SAML or OIDC connection itself is set up in your Auth0 tenant (docs/setup/sso.md); this page ties your domain to it. Sign-in through the connection does not by itself make anyone a member: use invitations, SCIM, or the option above.
